ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Shape and Reflectance Tokens from Posed Renders
PROPOSAL: Encode eight posed renders of each object into 256 latent tokens with a cross-attention encoder, then decode the tokens into a radiance field that takes the camera direction as an extra input. Train on a rendered Objaverse subset using raw meshes, with photometric and depth losses only, so that watertight conversion is never needed. Evaluate on held-out scanned household objects with peak signal-to-noise ratio, Chamfer distance and an error restricted to specular pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare Chamfer distance against a geometry-only autoencoder with the same token count and training renders. Compare specular error against a variant whose color ignores the camera direction. Run a published sparse-voxel structured latent on the same held-out objects. Repeat training with three seeds and give intervals.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Chamfer distance should stay within a few percent of the geometry-only autoencoder while specular error drops clearly against the direction-blind variant. The approach fails if geometry degrades beyond that range or if the specular gain disappears on glossy held-out objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Object Gaussian Token Autoencoder with Angular Reflectance
PROPOSAL: Represent each object as a fixed set of 1024 three-dimensional Gaussians whose color is a low-order spherical harmonic function of viewing direction, and learn an encoder that maps multiview images straight to the Gaussian parameters, trained end to end through a differentiable splatting renderer. Use a rendered Objaverse subset without mesh repair and hold out 500 objects for testing. Measure peak signal-to-noise ratio on unseen camera paths and Chamfer distance computed from rendered depth maps.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same encoder with color constrained to be constant in viewing direction, against a geometry-only point-cloud autoencoder with the same parameter count, and against a published two-stage structured latent on the same test objects, repeating each run with three seeds so that intervals can be given.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The direction-dependent version should gain several decibels over the constant-color version on glossy objects, with Chamfer distance close to the point-cloud reference. If the gains appear only on training objects, or if geometry worsens clearly, the idea fails.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orientation-Free Latent Generation from a Single Photograph
PROPOSAL: Fit a latent diffusion model over joint shape and appearance tokens, conditioned on one photograph through cross-attention, with object coordinates defined relative to the camera rather than a canonical dataset orientation. Initialise the denoiser from a pretrained image model, normalise the latents per channel, and train on rendered Objaverse objects. Judge silhouette overlap from the input viewpoint and the colour of highlights against the photograph.
CONTROLS: Compare with the same generator trained in canonical orientation and aligned afterwards, with a version conditioned on a colour-jittered photograph, and with a geometry-only generator, using three seeds for each.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Camera-relative coordinates should raise silhouette overlap and remove the alignment step, and highlight colour should track the photograph more closely than in the jittered variant. The approach falls short if overlap does not improve or if highlights drift from the lighting in the photograph.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Surface-Query Perceiver Autoencoder with Directional Radiance
PROPOSAL: Sample 16384 points on each raw mesh surface, attach colors gathered from multiview renders, and compress them with a Perceiver-style encoder into 128 learned latent tokens. A decoder answers queries of signed distance function (SDF) value and view-dependent radiance at any location and direction. Evaluate with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) and Chamfer distance, and score PSNR and LPIPS on specular regions separately.
CONTROLS: Compare SDF accuracy with a geometry-only autoencoder of equal token count, compare PSNR with a direction-blind decoder, and repeat everything with three seeds.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: PSNR and LPIPS on specular regions should improve over the direction-blind decoder while SDF accuracy stays close to the geometry-only model. The idea fails if specular gains are small or if geometry accuracy drops notably.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reflective Object Benchmark for Joint Latent Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Assemble a test set of 300 scanned and synthetic objects with mirror-like, brushed, rough and translucent surfaces, each rendered from 48 camera positions under two lighting conditions. Train a joint geometry-appearance latent autoencoder on a disjoint set and score it on this benchmark with image fidelity and Chamfer distance, stratified by material class.
CONTROLS: Compare against a geometry-only latent, against a latent whose appearance is view-independent, and against a published structured latent, stratifying every comparison by material class.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Gaps between direction-aware and view-independent latents should be largest on mirror-like and brushed surfaces and close to zero on rough matte ones. A flat gap across material classes would contradict the idea.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training on Raw Meshes versus Watertight Conversion
PROPOSAL: Train two identical joint autoencoders, one on renders of raw meshes and one on renders of meshes converted to watertight surfaces, and compare reconstruction quality together with total preparation effort. Measure preparation as processing time per object and as the number of failed conversions. Evaluate on held-out objects with photometric error, Chamfer distance and highlight error.
CONTROLS: Compare against a geometry-only autoencoder trained on each data variant, repeat with three seeds, and add a third variant that uses meshes simplified by half to check sensitivity to mesh quality.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Raw-mesh training should match the converted-mesh model within small differences while saving most of the preparation time. The idea fails if raw-mesh quality drops visibly on held-out objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token Count versus Fidelity in Compact Joint Latents
PROPOSAL: We train joint shape and appearance autoencoders with 32, 64, 128, 256 and 512 latent tokens on the same rendered corpus, and we trace fidelity and geometric accuracy against token count. We compare the curve with a dense voxel latent of comparable memory and with a geometry-only token model, and we inspect which regions lose detail first as tokens shrink.
CONTROLS: We repeat each configuration with three seeds, hold the decoder width fixed, and compare against the geometry-only model at each token count.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: We expect fidelity to saturate near 128 tokens, with highlights degrading first below that. We would regard the claim as failed if the curve is flat from 32 tokens upward, since that would show the evaluation is insensitive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Opacity and Transmission Channels for Translucent Objects
PROPOSAL: Extend the decoder of a joint latent with an opacity output and a transmission color output, then train on a small set of 400 translucent objects such as glass and wax rendered from varied angles. Compare reconstructions with and without the extra outputs on held-out translucent objects, scoring photometric error near edges and in thin parts.
CONTROLS: Run the decoder without the extra outputs, run a version trained on opaque objects only, and repeat all runs with three seeds.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: Translucent objects should show lower photometric error with the extra outputs, mainly near edges and thin parts. Gains that vanish on held-out glass would indicate failure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Inferring Scene Lighting for Single-Image Three-Dimensional Generation
PROPOSAL: Add a lighting encoder that predicts a compact environment code from the input photograph and feeds it to the latent generator, so that highlights in the output match the illumination in the photograph. Train on rendered objects under sampled environment maps and test on real photographs of glossy objects.
CONTROLS: Compare against a generator with no lighting code, against a generator given the true environment code, and against relighting the generated object afterwards.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The lighting code should place highlights closer to the photograph than the version without it, and approach the true-code version. Failure would appear as highlights that ignore the code on real photographs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Joint Latents on Real Scans
PROPOSAL: Start from a latent autoencoder pretrained on synthetic renders, then fine-tune it on captured real objects using photometric and depth supervision only, and check whether view-dependent fidelity survives the shift from synthetic to real data. Hold out whole captures for evaluation, measuring image fidelity, depth error and Chamfer distance against the captured geometry.
CONTROLS: Compare against the pretrained model without fine-tuning, against a model trained from scratch on the real scans, and against a geometry-only autoencoder fine-tuned the same way, with three seeds.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Fine-tuning should recover most of the fidelity lost on real scans, especially on glossy objects. The idea fails if the fine-tuned model overfits the captures and loses accuracy on held-out ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shape and Reflectance Tokens Learned from Multiview Renders
PROPOSAL: Encode eight posed renders per object into 256 latent tokens with a cross-attention encoder, then decode each token set into a radiance field that also takes the camera direction as input. Train on a rendered Objaverse subset using raw non-watertight meshes, with photometric and depth losses alone. Evaluate on held-out scanned household objects using peak signal-to-noise ratio, Chamfer distance and an error computed only over specular pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare Chamfer distance with a geometry-only autoencoder of matched token count trained on the same renders. Compare specular error with a variant whose color ignores the camera direction. Compare the metrics with a published sparse-voxel structured latent on the same held-out objects. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Chamfer distance should land within a few percent of the geometry-only autoencoder, with clearly lower specular error than the direction-blind variant. The claim fails if geometry degrades beyond that range or the specular gain vanishes on glossy held-out objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Photometric Object Tokens Trained from Posed Image Sets
PROPOSAL: Compress ten posed renders of each scanned object into 512 latent tokens using a perceiver-style encoder, and decode with a transformer that predicts color and density along rays given the ray direction. Optimize a photometric loss together with a depth term on a rendered Objaverse subset that skips mesh repair. Test on held-out household scans with peak signal-to-noise ratio, Chamfer distance and a specular-pixel error.
CONTROLS: Compare Chamfer distance with a geometry-only autoencoder of matched depth trained on the same renders. Compare specular error with a variant whose color head is twice as wide. Compare the metrics with a published text-conditioned shape latent on the same held-out objects. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Chamfer distance should settle within a few percent of the larger geometry-only autoencoder, with clearly lower specular error than the wider variant. The claim fails if geometry degrades beyond that range or the gain vanishes on glossy held-out objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: View-Conditioned Latent Autoencoder for Glossy and Translucent Objects
PROPOSAL: Build an autoencoder whose decoder receives a learned embedding of the viewing direction and returns color, opacity and depth for each ray cast through a compact set of 128 object tokens. Draw training data from raw scanned meshes rendered under several lighting conditions, with a split by object so that test shapes are unseen. Quantify fidelity with learned perceptual image patch similarity, depth error and Chamfer distance on points sampled from rendered depth.
CONTROLS: Vary the number of input views among few, moderate and many while the token count is held fixed. Compare a decoder given the viewing direction with one denied it. Compare the geometry against a geometry-only autoencoder trained on the same split. Repeat each run across seeds.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Specular detail should improve once the decoder sees the viewing direction, and fidelity should rise then flatten as input views increase. Failure shows up as an unchanged result when the direction input is removed or as geometry error rising above the geometry-only autoencoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compact Object Tokens with a Direction-Aware Rendering Decoder
PROPOSAL: Train an encoder-decoder that maps rendered views of a scanned object into 128 latent tokens, and decode them with a ray-based renderer that outputs color, opacity and depth using the camera direction as an additional input. Training renders use sampled lighting, and the evaluation split holds out whole objects. Score reconstructions with learned perceptual image patch similarity, depth error and Chamfer distance on points sampled from rendered depth.
CONTROLS: Vary the strength of image augmentation among weak, moderate and strong while the token count is held fixed. Compare a decoder with eight layers with one that has twelve. Compare the geometry against a geometry-only autoencoder trained on the same split. Repeat each run across seeds.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Fidelity should improve once augmentation is added, and quality should rise then flatten as decoder depth increases. Failure shows up as an unchanged result when augmentation is removed or as geometry error rising above the geometry-only autoencoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Appearance-Aware Latent Codes Evaluated on Glossy Subsets
PROPOSAL: Learn a set of latent tokens per object from posed renders, with a decoder that outputs signed distance and a direction-dependent color through a shared network. Build the training corpus from raw meshes with metallic, glossy and translucent materials, rendered under several environment lighting conditions. Assess accuracy by peak signal-to-noise ratio on novel camera angles and by Chamfer distance against the source meshes.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on a glossy and translucent test subset where highlights move with the camera. Compare against a geometry-only autoencoder with matched token count on that subset. Compare against a variant that averages color over views on that subset. Repeat the evaluation across lighting conditions.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: The direction-dependent decoder should reduce highlight error clearly on the glossy subset while Chamfer distance remains near the geometry-only reference. The idea fails if highlight error is unchanged on this subset or if geometry accuracy drops visibly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Shape Codes with an Angle-Dependent Shading Decoder
PROPOSAL: Fit per-object tokens from multiview renders, then run a single shared network over them to yield signed distance plus a color that depends on the viewing angle. The corpus consists of raw meshes made of matte, diffuse or printed-paper materials, lit by several environment maps. Accuracy is judged through peak signal-to-noise ratio on unseen camera angles and through Chamfer distance to the source meshes.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on a matte and opaque test subset where shading barely changes with the camera. Compare against a geometry-only autoencoder with matched token count on that subset. Compare against a variant that averages color over views on that subset. Repeat the evaluation across lighting conditions.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: The angle-dependent decoder should reduce shading error clearly on the matte subset while Chamfer distance remains near the geometry-only reference. The idea fails if shading error is unchanged on this subset or if geometry accuracy drops visibly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Geometry-Appearance Latents Judged by Highlight and Surface Error
PROPOSAL: Train a transformer encoder that turns sampled surface points and their multiview colors into 512 latent tokens, plus a decoder that answers queries for occupancy and view-dependent radiance at arbitrary points and directions. Use raw triangle meshes from Objaverse with camera positions drawn around each object, skipping watertight conversion. Hold out 1000 objects, then add a single-image generator on top of the frozen latents using a latent diffusion transformer.
CONTROLS: Measure highlight position error on held-out renders. Measure surface Chamfer distance against source meshes. Measure shape agreement from the input viewpoint for generated samples. Compare each against a geometry-only latent of matched token count, repeating with seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Highlight position error should fall clearly relative to a view-independent decoder, with surface distance unchanged within a small tolerance. The result fails if highlight error stays level or if generated shapes disagree with the input viewpoint.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transformer Latents for Surface Samples and Directional Radiance
PROPOSAL: Compress surface samples and per-view colors drawn from raw Objaverse triangle meshes into 512 learned tokens with a cross-attention encoder, while a lightweight decoder answers occupancy and radiance queries at arbitrary locations and directions. Cameras are placed around each object without mesh repair, and 1000 objects stay unseen. A latent diffusion transformer over the frozen tokens then produces objects conditioned on one image.
CONTROLS: Measure token usage entropy on held-out renders. Measure reconstruction loss against source meshes. Measure sample diversity for generated samples. Compare each against a geometry-only latent of matched token count, repeating with seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Token usage entropy should stay high relative to a view-independent decoder, with reconstruction loss unchanged within a small tolerance. The result fails if entropy collapses or if generated samples lack diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-Image Generation Checked Against the Input View and Lighting
PROPOSAL: Train a latent diffusion model on frozen joint shape and appearance tokens so that one photograph conditions the sampled object. Render each generated object from the input camera and from rotated cameras, with lighting estimated from the photograph. Use rendered Objaverse objects for training and 400 held-out real photographs of everyday objects for testing.
CONTROLS: Compare input-view silhouette overlap of the generated object with the photograph. Compare highlight appearance with a version relit by a different environment. Compare the single-stage generator with a two-stage pipeline that predicts coarse occupancy first. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Silhouette overlap with the photograph should be high, and highlights should follow the photograph's lighting rather than the swapped environment. The approach fails if the two-stage pipeline matches the shape and appearance of the single-stage generator closely, or if highlights ignore the lighting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional Object Sampling from One Image over Joint Latents
PROPOSAL: Fit a conditional latent diffusion model on frozen shape-and-appearance tokens, with one image as the sole condition for each sampled object. Generated objects are rendered from the input camera and from rotated cameras, with lighting estimated from the image. Training uses rendered Objaverse objects, while 400 held-out real photographs of everyday objects serve for testing.
CONTROLS: Compare input-view silhouette overlap of the generated object between seeds. Compare highlight appearance with a version recolored by a different palette. Compare the single-stage generator with a two-stage pipeline that predicts coarse occupancy first. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Silhouette overlap between seeds should be high, and highlights should stay consistent under the palette change rather than the lighting. The approach fails if the two-stage pipeline matches the single-stage generator closely, or if highlights differ erratically.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direction-Dependent Joint Latents Judged Against Geometry-Only Latents
PROPOSAL: Train an autoencoder that encodes sampled surface points and posed renders into 192 tokens and decodes occupancy together with a color that depends on viewing direction. Evaluate on glossy and translucent objects whose highlights shift between viewpoints, measuring geometry error against a geometry-only autoencoder and appearance error on specular pixels. Training uses raw meshes without watertight conversion.
CONTROLS: Match token count and training data between the joint and geometry-only models, hold out whole objects, and add a direction-blind variant of the joint model. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The joint model should keep geometry error close to the geometry-only autoencoder and reduce specular error clearly against the direction-blind variant. The direction fails if specular error does not move or if geometry degrades visibly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Faster Surface Extraction from Latent Object Codes
PROPOSAL: Develop a decoder for pretrained latent object codes that extracts triangle meshes through a coarse-to-fine octree query, so surface extraction needs far fewer network evaluations. Evaluate on 200 held-out objects by wall-clock extraction time, memory footprint and mesh agreement with the dense extraction. Training of the latent itself stays unchanged.
CONTROLS: Match latent codes and test objects between the octree and the dense extraction, hold out whole objects, and add a variant with a shallower octree. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Extraction time should drop sharply while mesh agreement stays close to the dense reference. The direction fails if agreement degrades visibly at the shallower octree or if speed gains vanish on detailed objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orientation-Free Single-Photograph Generation of Joint Latents
PROPOSAL: Train a latent diffusion transformer that generates object tokens conditioned on one photograph, using camera-relative coordinates so that outputs need no alignment to the view. Judge samples by silhouette overlap from the photograph's viewpoint, by highlight consistency with the photograph's lighting, and by plausibility of the geometry from rotated cameras. Test on 500 held-out photographs of glossy and matte objects.
CONTROLS: Compare with a generator trained in a canonical dataset orientation, hold the token autoencoder fixed, and add a variant given a downscaled photograph. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Silhouette overlap and highlight consistency should rise relative to the canonical-orientation generator, with diversity maintained. The direction fails if the two generators cannot be separated or if geometry collapses for unusual photographs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-Conditioned Generation Over Joint Geometry and Appearance Tokens
PROPOSAL: Fit a latent diffusion transformer that generates object tokens from a written description, using captions attached to rendered Objaverse objects. Judge samples by alignment between the caption and rendered views, diversity across prompts, and the plausibility of the geometry from rotated cameras. Test on 500 unseen captions covering materials, shapes and categories.
CONTROLS: Compare with a generator conditioned on category labels, hold the token autoencoder fixed, and add a variant with shorter captions. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Caption alignment should rise relative to the label-conditioned generator, with diversity maintained. The direction fails if alignment scores do not separate the two generators or if geometry collapses for rare prompts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lighting-Consistent Generation from One Photograph with Relit Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Train a generator on joint shape and appearance tokens conditioned on one photograph, then render each generated object under a rotated environment and compare against reference renders of the true object under that environment. Highlights, reflections and shading should shift correctly with the new lighting. Evaluate on 100 test objects with measured material properties.
CONTROLS: Compare against a generator that returns color independent of direction, compare against relighting a generated asset afterwards, and repeat across seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Relit renders should match the reference better than those from the direction-independent generator. The direction fails if generated highlights stay fixed under the new environment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Object Fitting from Dense Views to Measure Reconstruction Limits
PROPOSAL: Optimize a separate radiance field for each of 100 objects using fifty input views and a long iterative schedule, then record the best attainable image fidelity and geometry error on those views. Compare checkpoints across training length to find where gains stop. Every object receives its own optimization, so the result marks what a fitted representation can reach.
CONTROLS: Hold out views rather than objects, compare against a lower-view fit, and repeat across seeds.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Fidelity should keep rising with training length and the number of views until it saturates. The direction fails if the fitted fields overfit and lose accuracy on held-out views.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Joint Latents Directly from Raw Meshes and Renders
PROPOSAL: Build a pipeline that trains a joint geometry-appearance latent from unmodified meshes and rendered views, using sampled surface points and photometric loss with no signed-distance conversion or primitive fitting. Measure preparation time per object, failed samples, and the fidelity of the resulting latent on 300 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare against a pipeline that first converts meshes to watertight form, hold out objects, and repeat with seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Preparation time should fall sharply with fidelity close to the converted-mesh pipeline. The direction fails if raw-mesh training destabilises or loses accuracy on thin structures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Part-Level Editing Through Segmentation of Latent Object Tokens
PROPOSAL: Add a segmentation head to latent object tokens so that parts such as handles, lids and legs can be selected and replaced by swapping token subsets. Train the head on 300 annotated objects, then judge edits by part overlap and by rendered consistency of the untouched regions. Latent training itself reuses a pretrained autoencoder.
CONTROLS: Compare against segmentation on rendered images lifted to three dimensions, hold out annotated objects, and repeat with seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Part overlap should exceed that of the image-lifting alternative, with untouched regions preserved. The direction fails if edits leak across parts or consistency degrades.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compactness Versus Fidelity Against Voxel Latents for Single Objects
PROPOSAL: Train joint autoencoders with different token counts on the same objects, and place each point on a plot of memory footprint against reconstruction fidelity and geometry error. Compare against sparse and dense voxel latents at similar memory, using 150 held-out objects with glossy materials. The study asks where the token representation overtakes grids.
CONTROLS: Compare against sparse and dense voxel latents, hold out whole objects, and repeat with seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Token latents should reach similar fidelity to voxel grids with a smaller memory footprint. The direction fails if grids stay better at every memory level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scene-Scale Latents for Rooms with Many Objects
PROPOSAL: Train a latent autoencoder on indoor room scans containing dozens of objects, compressing each room into a fixed set of 768 tokens and decoding color and depth for novel viewpoints. Judge reconstruction by image fidelity and layout agreement on 150 held-out rooms. The study focuses on how large spaces rather than single objects are compressed.
CONTROLS: Compare against a voxel latent at room scale, hold out whole rooms, and repeat with seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Image fidelity should be comparable to the voxel latent with far fewer tokens. The direction fails if object detail disappears as the number of objects grows.
